Since I have top priority at schools x and z, I should rank one of them first. I value z higher than x, so I should rank z first.

Now, consider the remaining schools x, w, and y. I have priority 1 at x and priority 2 at w and y. Since z is already my top choice, I want to maximize my chances of getting into x if I don't get into z. Therefore, I should rank x second.

Now I need to decide between w and y. I value w higher than y, so I should rank w higher than y.

Therefore, my ranking should be z > x > w > y.

Let's consider if there are any dominated rankings. Suppose I ranked x first. If I get rejected from x, then I would be proposing to my second choice. If I ranked y first, I would be unlikely to get in since most applicants prefer y > x > w > z, and I only have priority 2. This is dominated by ranking z or x first.

Ranking w first is also dominated by ranking z or x first.

Therefore, the ranking z > x > w > y is not dominated.
